$comment: The class features of the 5th edition SRD for the classes in play, by the hero level they come at (the Skills tab lists them above the cantrips). kind: passive (on from the level it comes at; a click on its box switches it off and on), active (put on the quick bar like a spell and used with the cast key; cooldown is its recovery in seconds) or info (a rule, a choice or a proficiency: nothing to switch). worked: false means the game does not play it out yet; it is listed with the rest and says so. needs: 'protection' - only for a hero who took that fighting style. The Cleric's Divine Domain is Life. Subclasses the game does not have are left out. Ability Score Improvements and the fighting style are chosen in the level panel.

fighter.name: Fighting Style
fighter.description: You adopt a style of fighting as your specialty: Archery, Defense, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting or Protection. Pick it in the level panel (the badge by your level).

fighter.name: Protection
fighter.description: While you carry a shield, an enemy's attack on an ally within 5 feet of you is rolled with disadvantage. It needs 5 seconds to recover.

fighter.name: Second Wind
fighter.description: You draw on your stamina to heal yourself for 1d10 + your fighter level. In the tabletop game it recovers with a short or long rest; here it recovers in 30 seconds, and a rest restores it at once.

fighter.name: Action Surge
fighter.description: You push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment: every other ability and spell on your quick bar is ready again at once.

fighter.name: Extra Attack
fighter.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action. Three attacks at level 11, four at level 20.

fighter.name: Indomitable
fighter.description: You can reroll a saving throw that you fail. You must use the new roll. Two uses at level 13, three at level 17.

wizard.name: Spellcasting
wizard.description: You cast wizard spells with Intelligence. You learn more spells and open higher spell levels as you gain levels.

wizard.name: Arcane Recovery
wizard.description: You regain your focus: every spell on your quick bar is ready to cast again at once. In the tabletop game it is once a day, on a short rest; here it recovers in 2 minutes.

wizard.name: Spell Mastery
wizard.description: Choose a 1st-level and a 2nd-level wizard spell. You can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot.

wizard.name: Signature Spells
wizard.description: Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells as your signature spells. You can cast each once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot.

rogue.name: Expertise
rogue.description: Choose two of your skill proficiencies: your proficiency bonus is doubled for them. Two more at level 6.

rogue.name: Sneak Attack
rogue.description: +1d6 damage with a finesse or ranged weapon, one more die every two levels (the tabletop rule asks for advantage or an ally beside the target; in a real-time fight every such blow counts).

rogue.name: Thieves' Cant
rogue.description: You know the secret mix of dialect, jargon and code that lets you hide messages in seemingly normal conversation.

rogue.name: Cunning Action
rogue.description: Your quick thinking lets you Dash as a bonus action: your sprint stamina is full again at once.

rogue.name: Uncanny Dodge
rogue.description: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

rogue.name: Evasion
rogue.description: When you are subjected to an effect that allows a Dexterity saving throw for half damage, you take no damage if you succeed, and only half if you fail.

rogue.name: Reliable Talent
rogue.description: Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

rogue.name: Blindsense
rogue.description: If you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

rogue.name: Slippery Mind
rogue.description: You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

rogue.name: Elusive
rogue.description: No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren't incapacitated.

rogue.name: Stroke of Luck
rogue.description: If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, when you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.

warlock.name: Pact Magic
warlock.description: You cast warlock spells with Charisma. Your slots are few but always cast at your highest slot level (up to 5th); a short rest restores them. Your patron is the Fiend.

warlock.name: Eldritch Invocations
warlock.description: You gain eldritch invocations, fragments of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability. More at levels 5, 7, 9, 12, 15 and 18.

warlock.name: Agonizing Blast
warlock.description: Eldritch Blast adds your Charisma modifier to its damage.

warlock.name: Pact Boon
warlock.description: Your patron grants you a gift: the Pact of the Chain, the Blade or the Tome.

warlock.name: Mystic Arcanum
warlock.description: Your patron grants you a magical secret: a 6th-level spell, learnt at level 11. A 7th-level spell follows at level 13, an 8th at level 15 and a 9th at level 17. Each is cast at its own level only.

warlock.name: Eldritch Master
warlock.description: You can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power: every spell on your quick bar is ready to cast again at once. In the tabletop game it takes a minute of entreating your patron, once a day; here it recovers in 2 minutes.

bard.name: Spellcasting
bard.description: You cast bard spells with Charisma. You learn more spells and open higher spell levels as you gain levels.

bard.name: Bardic Inspiration
bard.description: You can inspire others through stirring words or music: an ally adds a d6 to one attack roll, ability check or saving throw. The die grows to d8 at level 5, d10 at level 10 and d12 at level 15.

bard.name: Jack of All Trades
bard.description: Half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) is added to initiative.

bard.name: Song of Rest
bard.description: Allies who regain hit points at the end of a short rest recover an extra 1d6. The die grows to d8 at level 9, d10 at level 13 and d12 at level 17.

bard.name: Expertise
bard.description: Choose two of your skill proficiencies: your proficiency bonus is doubled for them. Two more at level 10.

bard.name: Font of Inspiration
bard.description: You regain all of your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.

bard.name: Countercharm
bard.description: You can use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects: you and nearby allies have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed.

bard.name: Magical Secrets
bard.description: You have plundered magical knowledge from a wide spectrum of disciplines: you can learn spells from any class's list.

bard.name: Superior Inspiration
bard.description: When you roll initiative and have no uses of Bardic Inspiration left, you regain one use.

cleric.name: Spellcasting
cleric.description: You cast cleric spells with Wisdom. You learn more spells and open higher spell levels as you gain levels. Your Divine Domain is Life.

cleric.name: Disciple of Life
cleric.description: Your healing spells mend 2 + the spell's level more.

cleric.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
cleric.description: You present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy: a pool of 5 x your cleric level in hit points is shared among the allies within 30 feet (yourself included), none above half their hit points. In the tabletop game it recovers with a rest; here in 30 seconds.

cleric.name: Destroy Undead
cleric.description: When an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, it is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a threshold: 1/2 at level 5, 1 at 8, 2 at 11, 3 at 14 and 4 at 17.

cleric.name: Blessed Healer
cleric.description: When you cast a spell that restores hit points to another creature, you regain 2 + the spell's level hit points yourself.

cleric.name: Divine Strike
cleric.description: Your weapon strikes are infused with divine energy: +1d8 radiant damage with a weapon, 2d8 from level 14.

cleric.name: Divine Intervention
cleric.description: You can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.

cleric.name: Supreme Healing
cleric.description: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.
